skill.name: error-conversion-guide
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code on idiomatic Rust error conversion using From, thiserror, anyhow, map_err, and the ? operator.

content.value_statement: Rust error conversions can become repetitive and confusing across application layers. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward idiomatic From, map_err, anyhow, and thiserror patterns.
actual_capabilities: Recommends automatic error conversion with From and thiserror source variants.
Explains when to use manual From implementations for custom conversion logic.
Shows when map_err, anyhow context, boxed errors, and Result aliases are appropriate.
Guides layered error conversion between infrastructure, domain, and application boundaries.
Identifies common Rust error conversion mistakes that lose context or cause conflicts.
limitations: It does not compile, run, or test Rust code.
It focuses on Rust error conversion, not broad architecture review.
It depends on code snippets and compiler messages supplied by the user.
Project-specific error policies may require manual adaptation.

use_cases.title: Replace Repetitive Conversions
use_cases.description: Convert repeated map_err calls into cleaner automatic conversions when source errors map directly to application errors.

use_cases.title: Design Public Error Types
use_cases.description: Choose between thiserror, anyhow, boxed errors, and type aliases for library and application boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review Layered Services
use_cases.description: Map infrastructure, domain, and service errors without leaking low-level details across boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Manual Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust function and suggest a clearer error conversion pattern. Explain whether From, map_err, or anyhow fits best.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Question Mark Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve compiler errors from the ? operator.
prompt_templates.prompt: I get a Rust error when using the ? operator with two error types. Explain the missing conversion and suggest the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Enum
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan an application or library error type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an idiomatic Rust error enum for these operations and dependencies. Include guidance on automatic and manual conversions.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Layered Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these infrastructure, domain, and application errors. Propose a layered conversion strategy that preserves context and clear ownership.

output_examples.input: A parser reads a file, parses an integer, and uses repeated map_err calls for both failures.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single application error type with automatic conversions for file and parse errors, then explains when map_err is no longer needed.

output_examples.input: A service function combines repository, validation, and API client errors behind one result type.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a unified service error and explains how each lower-level error converts at the call site with the ? operator.

output_examples.input: An enum has two variants that both try automatic conversion from the same source error type.
output_examples.output: The skill explains why the conversion conflicts and recommends source-preserving variants with manual construction where context differs.

best_practices: Use automatic conversion when one source error clearly maps to one variant.
Preserve original error sources when callers need diagnostics or chaining.
Convert errors at architecture boundaries where terminology changes.
anti_patterns: Do not convert every error to a string before returning it.
Do not add multiple automatic conversions from the same source type.
Do not expose infrastructure errors directly from domain interfaces.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Rust code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples only. It does not compile, run, or test code.

faq.question: When should I use thiserror?
faq.answer: Use thiserror when you want specific error types, clear variants, and structured conversion support.

faq.question: When should I use anyhow?
faq.answer: Use anyhow in application code where flexible errors and added context are more important than public error types.

faq.question: Can it help with the ? operator?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains which From conversion is missing and how to make the operator work idiomatically.

faq.question: Does it replace project error policies?
faq.answer: No. It suggests Rust patterns, but project conventions and public API requirements still matter.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documentation-focused and supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
